## The semantic (verified empirically, claude 2.1.201, 2026-07-06)

A `PreToolUse` command hook can return
`hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput.command` to rewrite a Bash command before it
runs. The **permission deny patterns (`--disallowedTools 'Bash(git push:*)'`)
are then evaluated against the REWRITTEN command, not the one the model
issued.** Any rewriting hook therefore changes which deny patterns match.

Concretely, with the rtk token-filter hook active (it rewrites `git <sub>` →
`rtk git <sub>` for compressible subcommands — **including `git push`**):

- Probe: fresh `claude -p` session, `--dangerously-skip-permissions
  --disallowedTools 'Bash(git push:*)'`, asked to run `git push` in a
  throwaway repo → the command **EXECUTED** (failed only on "No configured
  push destination"). No deny fired.
- Control: same setup, `--disallowedTools 'Bash(touch:*)'`, a command rtk
  does NOT rewrite → **"Permission to use Bash … has been denied"**, file
  never created. So the deny mechanism works under
  `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; the push escape is pure pattern
  un-matching by the rewrite.

## Why it matters here

- Fleet spawns rely on `FLEET_DISALLOWED_TOOLS` (`Bash(git push:*)`,
  `Bash(sudo:*)`) as backstops (`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/invoke.ts`).
- rtk is installed on the dev box (and the Mac VM), so `rtk git push …` was a
  live manual evasion even before any fleet rtk-hook rollout — and a
  surface-B rollout (worker-plugin `hooks.json`) would have made it automatic.
- `Bash(sudo:*)` is NOT affected: rtk passes `sudo …` through unrewritten.

## The fix + the rule going forward

- **WI-3159** added `'Bash(rtk git push:*)'` to `FLEET_DISALLOWED_TOOLS`
  (+ a test pin in `invoke.test.ts`).
- **Rule:** whenever a command-REWRITING PreToolUse hook is added to any
  surface, re-derive the deny list: for every `Bash(<prefix>:*)` deny, ask
  "does the hook rewrite a command matching this prefix into one that no
  longer matches?" — if yes, deny the rewritten form too (or exclude that
  command from rewriting).
- Deny-side guards that must be rewrite-proof belong in a hook that runs
  BEFORE the rewriter and hard-denies (exit 2 / permissionDecision deny) —
  the shared-tree destructive-git guard already does this and is itself
  wrapper-hardened (it denies `rtk git reset --hard` etc., see the
  bash-resource-gate `_WRAP_STRIP` logic).

## Related

- The composition order on the dev box: guard hook first (deny wins), rtk
  second (rewrite) — `~/.claude/settings.json`.
- `invoke.ts` already documents command-string matching as evadable
  (`git -C … push`, aliases, `&& git push`); the repo pre-push hook remains
  the primary no-push enforcement for `main`. This insight adds the
  hook-rewrite variant to that list.
